editorialNarrative.hook: A rookie starts on pole: Zach Bates turns Bathurst's established order into a challenge for the full 1000 kilometres.
editorialNarrative.synopsis: Sunday's 161 laps at Mount Panorama close the Enduro Cup before the championship Finals. Ford's approved engine adjustment applies to Bathurst only; Chevrolet's separate ballast revision is a different technical measure. Driver handovers, reliability and race management now matter more than qualifying headlines. The grid is confirmed, not the result: no finishing order or Sunday outcome is assumed.
editorialNarrative.formCopy: Bates backed up Friday's record Gen3 qualifying lap by beating Brodie Kostecki in Saturday's Shootout. It is the first Bathurst pole for both the rookie and Matt Stone Racing. Kostecki starts alongside him; Anton De Pasquale is third. Broc Feeney, Cam Waters and Chaz Mostert missed the top ten, so several familiar contenders must build their challenge from further back.
editorialNarrative.closingCopy: For Matt Stone Racing, the front row makes an underdog story tangible without making Sunday a fairytale already won. Kostecki remains the immediate benchmark beside Bates. Toyota's Bend 500 breakthrough still offers a reason for its supporters to believe, but Mostert's grid position asks the team to earn that belief over the distance. One exceptional lap and a complete endurance performance are different achievements.
